data.title: Trump admin to review 'closed' AI models before release: reports
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO (UNITED STATES) - The Trump administration on Tuesday met with tech leaders to finalise a security review process for advanced AI models before their release, though it will apply only to "closed" models, US media reported.

data.title: 'Like the end of the world': the eclipse chasers flocking to Spain
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Suddenly, the world is plunged into an eerie, violet darkness. The temperature drops. Birds and other animals, bewildered by unforeseen night, start behaving strangely. Stars and planets appear in the sky next to the blotted-out Sun.

data.title: UK mansion where 'listeners' spied on Nazi generals becomes museum
data.description: ENFIELD — Upstairs, Nazi generals enjoyed wine and lounged in elegant rooms. Downstairs in the basement, a team of covert listeners followed their chatter, gleaning vital insights into Germany's war plans.

data.title: High bills, cheap panels drive a Philippine solar surge
data.description: MANILA - Edwin Salas watched as the first of 20 solar panels was installed on the roof of his home, joining a Philippine solar energy boom sent into overdrive by the Middle East war.

data.title: SpaceX rocket stage expected to slam into Moon
data.description: NEW YORK - A SpaceX rocket's upper stage is set to unintentionally crash into the Moon on Wednesday, a collision that poses no danger to Earth but will leave behind a lunar crater.

data.title: Trump's sale of access to Truth Social raises eyebrows
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump's move to charge for early access to his often market-moving Truth Social posts is raising eyebrows a year and a half into an administration that has already seen unprecedented enrichment for the First Family.

data.title: Italian garbagemen help recover lost 1 mln euro lottery ticket
data.description: ROME - A one-million-euro lottery ticket was recovered from the trash in Italy after the frantic winner called on garbagemen to help her retrieve it, the waste management company told AFP.

data.title: EU nations patch things up after Ceuta migration discord
data.description: BRUSSELS (BELGIUM) - Spain and fellow EU nations moved to bury the hatchet Tuesday after a mass influx of migrants into the North African enclave of Ceuta laid bare fault lines on migration within the 27-nation bloc.

data.title: Tiny Pacific island nation reclaims traditional name
data.description: SYDNEY - ⁠The ⁠Pacific island nation of Nauru ​has officially changed its name to ​the Republic of Naoero, reverting ‌to its traditional designation in a move it said was aimed at strengthening national identity and cultural heritage.

data.title: Guatemala issues 'danger' alert after Fuego volcano erupts
data.description: GUATEMALA CITY — Guatemalan authorities issued the country's second-highest emergency alert level on Monday after a major eruption of Central America's most active volcano, prompting the evacuation of nearby villages.

data.title: Arson suspect arrested as US northwest battles wildfires
data.description: SPOKANE (UNITED STATES) — US authorities arrested a man Monday on suspicion of arson in connection with the biggest of three fires burning around the northwestern city of Spokane, as firefighters raced to contain flames that have displaced tens of thousands.

data.title: Myanmar ex-junta chief set for first Thailand visit as civilian leader
data.description: NAY PYI TAW — Myanmar's ex-junta chief Min Aung Hlaing is expected in Thailand on Thursday, making his first trip there since becoming civilian leader as he seeks a return to the diplomatic fold for his pariah state.

data.title: ANA flight makes evasive manoeuvre before landing at Tokyo's Haneda airport
data.description: An All Nippon Airways flight from Shanghai made an evasive manoeuvre while approaching Haneda airport around 6am (4am Thailand time) on Tuesday, the company said.

data.title: Britain's Royal Mint strikes gold in electronic waste
data.description: LLANTRISANT (WALES) - At the heart of Britain's coin factory, old Bank of England telephones are stripped down and dipped into giant vats to recover a hidden treasure: the gold in their circuits.

data.title: Trapped by war, Bangladesh seafarer recounts Gulf ordeal
data.description: DHAKA - For 115 days, captain Mohammad Shafiqul Islam was stranded on the high seas of the Gulf, watching missiles light up the night sky and rationing food and water for his crew.

data.title: North Korea advises citizens to eat dog meat to beat the summer heat
data.description: SEOUL — North Korea’s state media has recommended dog meat soup as protection against summer heat, reviving Pyongyang’s long-running effort to promote the controversial dish as record high temperatures grip both sides of the Korean peninsula.

data.title: Ships passing through key Gulf waterways amid uncertain peace talks
data.description: SINGAPORE - Shipping ⁠traffic ⁠at the key Gulf ​waterways of Bab el-Mandeb and Strait of Hormuz held largely ​unchanged at the ‌start of the week, shipping data showed, as the progress of talks between the United States and Iran remained ambiguous.

data.title: South Korea's heatwave kills 16
data.description: SEOUL — South ⁠Korean President ​Lee Jae Myung urged on Tuesday ​authorities to ‌step up support for people affected by a record heatwave in the country, saying the death toll had ​risen ⁠to 16 and warning that extreme weather was becoming more frequent.

data.title: WWII shells surface in wildfire-ravaged French village
data.description: LE PORGE (FRANCE) - A huge forest fire near Bordeaux in southwestern France has revealed World War II shells in the village of Le Porge, where all residents returned to their homes on Monday after days of demining operations.
